correctness.rationale: For each of the two explicitly defined 16-vertex 6-regular graphs, the primary algorithm constructs all 65536 successors, exhaustively decomposes the finite functional graph, and checks each class without sampling. An independently built coordinate/sign implementation tests every initial state for its first fixed or 2-periodic iterate, yielding precisely the same six/eight nonzero classes, weights, cycle totals and sharp depths; explicit witnesses 359 and 1901 attain depths 3 and 5. The third checker verifies adjacency-square identity and the 4-clique/fixed-four-state structural witness. All counts sum to 65536 per graph; no infinite conclusion follows.

value.rationale: The two unique nonisomorphic strongly regular mates (16,6,2,2) form a canonical comparison with identical spectrum. Their complete binary-majority temporal profiles differ in fixed-state count, primitive two-orbit count and sharp time-to-period, none of which is imposed by the known spectrum or general period-two theorem. A structural 4-clique distinction explains one component, while the complete exact nonlinear census gives meaningful benchmark invariants. A natural complete finite classification can stand without an all-graph generalization.
